blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: **переносишь** is the present tense (2nd person singular) of **переносить** (to transfer, to carry, to transport (somewhere); to carry over (a word) to the next line) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **перенести**. present: я переношу́ · ты перено́сишь · он перено́сит · мы перено́сим · вы перено́сите · они перено́сят. — Wiktionary, «переносить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  «Переносить — перенести — to carry over (on foot), to move; to endure.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Перенесите этот стол в мою комнату.» (to move) — DLI, Lesson 79. «В прошлом году я перенёс тяжёлую болезнь.» (to endure) — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **введите** is the imperative (вы, plural or polite) of **ввести** (to introduce; to bring in, to usher in) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вводить**. imperative: введи́ · введи́те. — Wiktionary, «ввести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **придёт** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. future: я приду́ · ты придёшь · он придёт · мы придём · вы придёте · они приду́т. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **зашёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. past: он зашёл · она зашла́ · оно зашло́ · они зашли́. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I came by to check on you.
exercises.context: **за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **уходить** (the infinitive) (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **уйти**. — Wiktionary, «уходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **вылетит** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **вылететь** (to fly out, to fly (from a place); (computing) to crash) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вылетать**. future: я вы́лечу · ты вы́летишь · он вы́летит · мы вы́летим · вы вы́летите · они вы́летят. — Wiktionary, «вылететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **приезжай** is the imperative (ты, singular) of **приезжать** (to arrive, to come (by vehicle or horse)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **приехать**. imperative: приезжа́й · приезжа́йте. — Wiktionary, «приезжать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Приходите and приезжайте both mean "come" (on foot, by vehicle). Идите means both "go" and "come" (on foot), and is used only when immediate action of the person (who is normally in sight) is expected. Compare:.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «The familiar form of the imperative does not have the ending -те: войдите — войди, идите — иди, приезжайте — приезжай, приходите — приходи.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда? — Это старшина. Лейтенант в штабе? — Нет, он уже идёт (едет) сюда.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Он всегда приезжает сюда на грузовике.» (Imperfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Он всегда приезжал сюда на грузовике.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Drop everything and get over here.
exercises.context: Приходите and приезжайте both mean "come" (on foot, by vehicle). (DLI, Lesson 24)

exercises.why: **привела** is the past tense (feminine) of **привести** (to bring (someone with)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приводить**. past: он привёл · она привела́ · оно привело́ · они привели́. — Wiktionary, «привести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **привести**: to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road); to result, to lead, to bring; (mathematics) to reduce.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «приводить — привести — to bring (along), to lead.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: The drought led to an insufficiency of food.
exercises.context: The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. (DLI, Lesson 79)

exercises.prompt: He ran away with his tail between his legs.
exercises.context: **у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **вынести** (the infinitive) (to carry out, to take out, to bring out, to remove; to transfer) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выносить**. — Wiktionary, «вынести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. exercises.prompt: I have to take out the trash.

exercises.why: **сбежать** (the infinitive) (to run down (from); to run away, to make off, to flee, to break out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сбегать**. — Wiktionary, «сбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **с-, со-** — Movement downwards. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **подошло** is the past tense (neuter) of **подойти** (to approach, to come to, to walk to, to draw near [with к (k)]; to fit, to suit, to match, to be right [with dative]) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **подходить**. past: он подошёл · она подошла́ · оно подошло́ · они подошли́. — Wiktionary, «подойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**под-, подо-** — Approach. Antonym: от- Example: Он подошёл к девушке, чтобы спросить её номер. — He approached the girl to ask for her number. Prepositional phrases: к + dat.; до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix под- denote approaching to an object, a place or a person and require the preposition к + dative case: Я подхожу к столу. Рядовой подходит к сержанту. Мы подъезжаем к городу.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **под-, подо-** — Approach. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
